name: Cinder's Lament

stars.name: The Mourner
stars.notes: Brown dwarf too small to sustain hydrogen fusion. Slowly cooling over billions of years, current surface temperature approximately 1,800 K. Barely visible even from its innermost planet—more felt as warmth than seen as light.

planets.name: Vigil
planets.notes: Cold world with methane and nitrogen ice surface, orbiting at just 0.03 AU. Even this close to its star, surface temperature averages -140°C. Faint infrared glow from The Mourner tints the ice fields a permanent deep red.

planets.name: Forgetting
planets.notes: Airless rock in perpetual near-darkness. Surface features are known only from radar mapping—visible light from The Mourner is insufficient for optical observation. Contains a field of identical stone pillars, each 12 meters tall, arranged in a grid pattern across 40 square kilometers.

anomalies.name: The Pillar Field
anomalies.notes: 2,401 stone pillars arranged in a 49x49 grid with 28-meter spacing. Each pillar is carved from local basalt to identical dimensions. The grid is oriented precisely toward galactic north. Erosion patterns suggest an age of 3-4 billion years, though the absence of atmosphere on Forgetting means erosion agents are limited to micrometeorite impacts.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed and essentially unknown. The system appears in brown dwarf catalogs but has never been the subject of a dedicated mission.

history: The Mourner was catalogued in 2334 as part of a brown dwarf census. Its planets were detected by infrared transit in 2371 but not physically surveyed.

A prospecting vessel passing through the region in 2498 conducted a cursory radar scan of Forgetting and detected the Pillar Field. The discovery was filed with the Exploration Guild database but generated no follow-up interest due to the system's extreme remoteness and lack of economic potential.
No crewed expedition has ever visited Cinder's Lament. All knowledge of the system comes from automated probes and the single prospector's scan. The Pillar Field remains unexamined by human eyes.
description: Cinder's Lament is one of the darkest inhabited star systems in the catalog—though 'inhabited' is generous. The Mourner is a brown dwarf, a failed star that never achieved sustained fusion, and it has been slowly cooling for nearly eight billion years. Its light is a deep magenta-red warmth barely distinguishable from infrared, and its two worlds exist in a state of perpetual twilight that shades into absolute darkness. Vigil is a ball of colored ice. Forgetting is a rock so dark that only radar can map it. Between them, they orbit a star that is slowly forgetting how to glow.

The Pillar Field on Forgetting is known only from a single radar scan conducted by a prospector who never returned. Forty-nine rows of forty-nine pillars, carved from local stone, oriented to galactic north, standing in the dark for billions of years. No one has examined them up close. No one has tested their composition, measured their inscriptions if any exist, or determined whether they serve a purpose beyond standing in perfect geometric silence on a world where no one can see them. They are a monument built in darkness for an audience of none.

This is a system at the edge of relevance—too dim to attract attention, too remote to justify expeditions, too poor to reward investment. The Pillar Field is a footnote in a database, a curiosity that has not risen to the level of mystery because no one has bothered to be curious. The Mourner continues its slow descent toward absolute cold. The pillars continue to stand. And somewhere in the lightless gap between the two, the question of who built them and why waits for someone who may never come.
